attacks.claim: After CallNotify ends on 2027-03-31, the fallback and STOP paths restore patrons to phone, a channel that will no longer exist. New SMS sign-ups are also written with NOTICE_PREV=phone. The rollback's print target is not in scope, built, or costed, and the replacement channel is explicitly out of scope (LIBSYS-330), so the no-lost-notices constraint is not met for these patrons.
attacks.evidence: 'new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`' and 'restore `NOTICE_PREV` (email or phone call; print notice once CallNotify has ended)'; ABSENT: any print-notice build item in Section 2 or 7, and any rule for NOTICE_PREV=phone after 2027-03-31. 'what replaces calls for patrons who stay on phone after March 2027 (LIBSYS-330)' is Out of scope.

attacks.claim: The template discloses that a hold exists, with branch and pickup date, to whatever number is on file. The plan's claim that a reassigned or shared number reveals nothing is contradicted by its own template, and the statute bars disclosing requests. No reassigned-number check or legal review of the template is documented.
attacks.evidence: 'A reassigned number or shared phone reveals nothing about what the patron requested.' vs '1 item is ready for pickup at Eastside Branch until Nov 4'; ABSENT: reassigned-number detection, re-consent, or legal review of the template.

attacks.claim: The public webhook changes consent and channel state for many patrons, but the signature algorithm, secret storage and rotation, timestamp window and replay protection are all unspecified. A forged or replayed STOP or status callback could flip channels across shared numbers.
attacks.evidence: 'exposes a single rate-limited POST path, verifies the provider's request signature, then: switches every patron whose SMS number matches'; ABSENT: signature algorithm, secret handling, replay or nonce check.

attacks.claim: 10DLC approval is expected around 3–10 November, before Week 4, but the plan has no rejection or amendment path. It also does not say whether the Week 3 staff pilot can send before campaign approval, since carriers can block unregistered traffic.
attacks.evidence: 'submitted Oct 20; typical approval is 1–3 weeks. Public launch is gated on approval.' and 'Week 3: staff pilot.' ABSENT: pilot send path, rejection plan, decision date.

attacks.claim: The $600 approved SMS cap is breached at roughly 1.7x assumed uptake (about 52,800 texts, or about $600), and the 2x case reaches about $690. The only control is a $450 alert that depends on someone reading it, with no send cap or auto-pause.
attacks.evidence: 'Approved notices budget allows up to $600/month for SMS (finance memo FIN-2026-117); a provider spend alert fires at $450.' ABSENT: send cap or auto-pause. 'Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons'

attacks.claim: The guarantee that patrons end up on exactly the channel they had before is unsupported. The plan has no rule for writing NOTICE_PREV on re-enrolment after STOP or on a manual OPAC channel change, so restoration can point at SMS or a stale channel, which also undermines rollback.
attacks.evidence: 'Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before.' ABSENT: NOTICE_PREV write rule on re-enrolment or manual channel change.

attacks.claim: The city attorney reviewed only the provider's DPA and confidentiality clause. The hold-filled text, HELP text, confirmation text, Spanish template and desk consent flow have no documented review against the library-records statute.
attacks.evidence: 'a library-records confidentiality clause reviewed by the city attorney (Oct 1)'; ABSENT: legal review of the SMS message, HELP text, confirmation text, Spanish text, or desk flow.

attacks.claim: When a failed-delivery callback queues the NOTICE_PREV notice, the original SMS row may still be pending or be retried, so the patron could get duplicate notices. The plan does not say whether the original row is suppressed.
attacks.evidence: 'on an `undelivered`/`failed` status callback, the receiver queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel'; ABSENT: suppression of the original pending SMS row.

attacks.claim: Fan-out is keyed only on phone number with no cap or batch limit, and a desk-entered number has no ownership check. One STOP from a shared or reassigned number can change channels for patrons who did not opt out.
attacks.evidence: 'switches every patron whose SMS number matches (family members can share a phone)' and 'staff set it at the desk when the patron asks and provides a mobile number'; ABSENT: fan-out cap, number ownership check.

attacks.claim: Desk-set SMS_CONSENT records a staff source but no patron-attested consent wording, and the disclosures (STOP, rates) arrive only in a confirmation text sent after recording.
attacks.evidence: 'Patron attribute `SMS_CONSENT` records the date and source (opac/desk).' and 'On enrolment, Koha sends one confirmation text'

attacks.claim: Provider delivery metadata (phone number, timestamp, and branch/date in the body during transit) is kept 90 days and can link a number to library hold activity. The plan relies on contract terms and does not analyse this against the statute.
attacks.evidence: 'Message bodies are redacted at the provider after delivery; delivery metadata is kept 90 days per contract.'

attacks.claim: Receiver logs keep last-4 digits alongside the Koha message id and timestamp, which can be joined to patron records. Log retention and read access are not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'Webhook receiver logs status, Koha message id and timestamp only' and 'phone numbers as the last 4 digits'; ABSENT: log retention and access list.

attacks.claim: The 'config change, not code change' claim is understated. STOP keyword handling, webhook signature verification and 10DLC registration are all provider-specific, so switching providers needs code and re-registration work.
attacks.evidence: 'Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change.' vs 'verifies the provider's request signature' and 'the provider handles carrier-required keyword replies'

attacks.claim: The $0.011 per-text rate has no cited quote, so the whole budget rests on an unsourced figure. The SMS spend also continues after March 2027 when the call saving ends, and the plan sets no review date.
attacks.evidence: '~$0.011 per text including carrier fees → ~$335/month' and 'Calls drop by ~20,500/month → ~$2,250/month saved while CallNotify runs.'

attacks.claim: The ≤5.5% expiry target is not derived. The 9.2% vs 5.1% gap compares phone and email populations rather than channels, and the 40-staff pilot is not representative of uptake.
attacks.evidence: 'Uncollected-hold expiry rate for SMS patrons ≤ 5.5% (phone today: 9.2%).' and '40 staff cardholders opt in'

attacks.claim: Accented Spanish vowels (á, í, ó, ú) fall outside GSM-7, which moves those messages to UCS-2 and halves the segment length. The one-segment and per-text cost claims are unverified for Spanish, and the Spanish body is absent. HELP and the confirmation text are also English-only.
attacks.evidence: 'Template (English, plus Spanish for patrons whose preferred language is Spanish, via `TranslateNotices`), GSM-7, one segment'; 'HELP auto-reply (configured at the provider)'; ABSENT: Spanish text and encoding check.

attacks.claim: Fallback and STOP handling depend on receiver callbacks, but no alert fires if the receiver goes down or callback volume drops to zero. Notices could then disappear silently.
attacks.evidence: 'Delivery rate ≥ 97% (provider status callbacks).' ABSENT: alerting on receiver downtime or zero callback volume.

attacks.claim: Rollback is tested only against a staging copy, not production volume. Step 2 re-queues pending rows but cannot recall messages the provider has already accepted, so some patrons will get both an SMS and a restored notice.
attacks.evidence: 'written and tested in week 2 against a staging copy of the patron database' and 'Re-queue any pending SMS rows in `message_queue` on the restored channel'

attacks.claim: The receiver's DB grants are broader than its stated function. UPDATE on borrower_attributes and INSERT on messages would let a compromised receiver rewrite patron attributes and inject messages.
attacks.evidence: 'uses a dedicated DB user with UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`'

attacks.claim: The custom receiver writes directly to Koha core tables but names no owner, test suite, or upgrade-coupling check.
attacks.evidence: 'A webhook receiver (~150 lines, on the existing Koha app server behind the existing nginx/TLS)'; ABSENT: owner, tests, upgrade coupling.
